VRChat has come a long way.

As a Denizen of VRChat for over 10K Hours as of writing this, Exactly 11,750.

It's a great escape, it's a secondary life. But, it also comes with a large wallet price, a price even to your own sanity, obsession, and quite possibly a horrible yet wonderful addiction.

There's a lot of good qualities that make you want to consume more content on VRChat's almost limitless possiblities of avatars, worlds, and recreations of just about anything you can think of... Think of it like Media Molecules; Little Big Planet but Virtual and you can practically just do whatever.

And there's a HUGE amount of bad as well, people who don't know face value of knowing reality from fiction. The onset of literally on going cases of groomers, preds, drama groups, trolls, and quite the whole kaboodle of anything second life related as well. (Yes, there's even people who roleplay entire families and never quite met a single stable one...)

You will meet people of all kinds of life, living their alternate dream life of who they want to be, represent who they are and you might end up being in this circle somehow and in some way.

I started as a Deskie, worked to questie, and now... a full body thottie. 

I came here to enjoy a secondary life of fun, quick adventures... Now, over the 10 years... *Yes, technically this was before 2017, it was a alpha back then.* It became a part of my life.

I highly recommend to enjoy this with friends first, don't rush in gettin' a headset unless you're ready to join in the fun and highly addicting social meta this brings to you.

If you're going solo, I just strongly say this to you. Go solo for a while, explore worlds, check games, and see what it has to offer before going social. And if you're an adult, PLEASE just get Age Verification. It helps immensely, if you a rig that can run this game, you got 10$ to spare to verify. 

I recommend it, but if you truly want to waste/enjoy your life. VRChat is for you, it *literally* welcomes any person... 

But don't be like me... Please, moderate your time and resources elsewhere! 11k + hours... MY GOD, LET ME OUT!

for a game that's made to bring people together, it rly lacks the necessary tools and the proper environment to help regular and new users find their circle/group that they are most comfortable with. it's pretty common finding a floater that usually appears once or twice, adds you as a friend once before never showing up again. not only is it difficult to find the group you feel like you belong into, it's difficult (esp to new users) to even attempt fitting in these groups due to the trust rank system the game subjects everyone under. the same system that helps players rule out trollers, crashers, client users, etc. is the same system that prevents new users from finding these groups. 

not to say that the trust rank system doesn't help, in almost every case, it really does in the sense that it stops bad actors from crashing the party. it also makes new users work a tiny bit in order to confirm whether or not they are deserving of more access(?) to the platform.

another thing is that, yes.. many issues involve new users. for someone trying out vrchat, their usual instinct is to try out the more popular worlds, worlds that are more often than not toxic. there are many games on the popular/active page that rly grinds my gears due to the communities that inhabit them, i mean, it's reeeeally bad. from my observations, the worst one may be 1's optimized box. the game itself is crawling w e-gangsters, e-daters, depraved users (ones vrc is commonly known for having a lot of, iykyk), disgusting people that threaten to pull your personal info n whatnot. anyway, my point is that a lot of these new users are exposed to these harsher environments since they're pretty much just thrown into the game with no direction whatsoever, assumably making them p much click on anything w/ the most playercount. vrc itself as far as i know doesn't care as long their users aren't exposed to anything harmful, which in this case, these players still would be. 1's optimized box is craaawling with them, it's even worse when the cesspit itself is a tight-knit community where the same people are able to find each other more often than not. mix all that in with the fact that most of these players are lonely people who are desperate for friends, people who might be in the wrong headspace prone to whatever sort of harm vrc staff is trying to prevent.

the game rly js needs better tools, a better system of sorts that allows people to find groups that are actually active n easily accessible, groups these users will be most comfortable with. now, i'm not really a merchant of ideas but these are some issues i think that can rly be resolved, issues that i think have plausible solutions to fixing. not that i have the thorough thinking to come up with these solutions, but i think i'm able to address them thorough enough for smth to be worked on.

there are definitely a handful more problems w/ the very depraved community, the lacking presence of staff, and whatever problem many users have already brought up. rather than repeating what's already known, i want to bring under light an actual observation of mine.

Let me start with the score, because I know you saw it and got confused: 6/10. This is a game I've played for 145 hours over the course of seven years. Those two facts coexist because VRChat is less of a game and more of a very weird third place that occasionally crashes.

The 6 is earned honestly. It's buggy in ways that stopped surprising me years ago — things clip through things, avatars break, and the whole thing runs on Unity versions so old that half of them probably qualify for a pension. The avatar ecosystem is an archaeology project: "does this model still work" is a genuine gamble, and someone out there is keeping a 2018 model alive through sheer willpower and outdated shaders. Respect, honestly.

But here's the thing: none of that has ever mattered once I'm actually in a world. Murder 4 with my friends has permanently destroyed our ability to trust each other, and I genuinely cannot count how many times The Black Cat turned "random person in a lobby" into "person I've now known for years." It's the digital equivalent of a neighborhood pub, except the regulars include dragons, anime girls, and at least one guy who hasn't moved from the same couch since 2020.

So: 6/10 as software. 9/10 as a place. The tech is held together with duct tape, but somehow that duct tape has friends on it.

im not someone who goes into public instances, for me this game is pretty much entirely for playing with my friends and especially with my partner. i go off in one room in our house, they go off in another, and we just get to play around exploring pretty worlds, playing fun games and generally having a great time being our favorite characters

I think what someone will feel about this game will entirely depend on their use-case for it. if you're someone who, like me, just wants to play it with people you already know it's fantastic! I've always been someone that loves getting lost in fantasy worlds anyway, this is the game that convinced me to get a vr headset, and to try out building a cheap full body tracking setup entirely to further immerse myself. there's a slew of absolutely beautiful user created worlds, free avatars, and games to play that realistically you could play VRC and never spend a dime. it has inspired me, though, to further learn things like making custom avatars just because it feels so good to get to be my favorite characters that I'd love to go further, play dress-up, even make some of my own characters.

youll find annoying people in public rooms in any multiplayer game, it's the curse of MMOs. someone trying too hard to be funny, someone who's genuinely just really mean. if that's not for you, id recommend going my way and just finding a group of buddies and hanging out in fun worlds, exploring, and getting immersed. that isn't the fault of the game itself, but a symptom of the very fact it's multiplayer game with public chatrooms. but since you could easily never go public, I highly recommend it, and in fact is quite possibly one of the coolest VR user generated platforms I've gotten to experience.
